finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the unsanitized query parameter f is joined onto /srv/files and read with os.ReadFile, so an unauthenticated remote attacker can read any file the process can read (for example f=../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd).
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with root = "/srv/files" (const at files.go:9); response body written at files.go:18

trace.note: name is taken verbatim from query parameter f; no decoding, allow-listing, or validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") lexically cleans to "/etc/passwd"; Join does not confine the result under root
os.ReadFile opens and reads the resolved path; symlinks under root are also followed
file contents are returned to the requester via w.Write(data)
/dl is registered on the default mux and served by ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) at line 34 with no middleware, so no authentication or authorization guards the route

finding.guards_checked: No input validation (no rejection of '..', absolute paths, or NUL bytes). No filepath.Clean plus strings.HasPrefix containment check. No filepath.EvalSymlinks or os.Root (Go 1.24+) containment. No authentication or authorization on the route. The only error path (files.go:14-16) maps read failures to 404 and does not restrict successful reads. Impact is read-only, but it discloses arbitrary host files including credentials and secrets, so severity is high. Fix: reject names containing '..' or path separators, or use os.OpenRoot(root) and root.Open(name) (Go 1.24+); add authentication if the endpoint is not meant to be public.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12-13 takes the query parameter f verbatim and passes filepath.Join(root, name) straight to os.ReadFile. No '..' rejection, no Clean plus prefix containment check, no os.OpenRoot, and no auth. The only error path (files.go:14-17) maps failures to 404 and does not restrict successful reads. The filepath.Base sanitization at files.go:22 applies only to the separate /avatar handler, not /dl.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the source: files.go:12 reads f verbatim, files.go:13 joins it onto /srv/files and calls os.ReadFile, files.go:18 writes the bytes to the response, and files.go:32-34 registers /dl on the default mux served on :8082 with no middleware. filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", so an anonymous network client can read arbitrary files the process can read.
